title: Choose the Super Administrator control-room structure
question: All three keep RetailMind’s operational identity. Choose how rapid triage and guided resolution should share the screen.

options.label: Radar + Resolution
options.lineage: risk radar paired with an incident workbench
options.thesis: Scan every risk at once, then resolve the selected issue without leaving the control panel.
options.viewport: A compact risk horizon sits above a ranked queue and a persistent three-step resolution workbench.
options.risk: The split workspace needs disciplined density to remain calm on smaller screens.

options.label: Guided Escalation Spine
options.lineage: runbook sequence with persistent system context
options.thesis: Turn the dashboard into a deliberate path from detection through verification and resolution.
options.viewport: The current highest-risk issue anchors a vertical resolution sequence while remaining risks stay in a compact side queue.
options.risk: Excellent guidance, but slower than the other structures for scanning many simultaneous conditions.

options.label: Operations Desk
options.lineage: two-pane administrative desk with a shared status ledger
options.thesis: Keep the ordered exception list and technical controls visible as one stable daily workspace.
options.viewport: A dense ordered exception register occupies the left half; the right half holds actions, access readiness, and system context.
options.risk: The familiar administrative structure is dependable but less distinctive than the other two.
